title: The orbital works: once SOL-88 is up the ARC-01 launches a collector at the start of every sector after a secured one; each is a light on a ring in the sky and seconds of beam for SOL; the launch has the rocket thrust bed
context: Owner, 2026-10-02: "we have 100 minutes and lots of fable credits before the reset. let's do something big." The direction of 2026-09-24 (a self-sustaining colony building toward a Dyson sphere) had its own spec owed; the ARC-01 and the SOL-88 launch of 2026-10-01 made a first slice cheap. Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-02-orbital-works-design.md.
outcome: src/domain/orbital-works.js (launchDue: online, standing launcher, the sector before secured, one on the sled at a time, one a sector; energyBonus capped) with src/content/orbital-works.js (2 s a collector, cap 20 s; the ring 1.9 radii out, tilted 28 degrees, 48 lights). src/fx/orbital-ring.js is one Points draw whose draw range is the collectors in orbit; the programme host runs the launch with the arrival's rocket_thrust bed under the charge, the release and the climb; the arsenal's ordinary passes carry the bonus (setEnergyBonus); the books count `launch` events (colony.launches: SOL-88 and the collectors) and the debrief shows ARC-01 LAUNCHED and IN ORBIT on THE COLONY HOLDS. Found on the way: the strip did not rename to SOL-88 under a held clock (the station now refreshes it on setAuto), and the host read the sector reports off the wrong object (a frame fault froze the laser's clock while the state hook kept answering). --colony extended: a secured sector, the next begun, the collector up, the ring at one, pass energy 15 -> 17.
alternatives: Launching on every secured sector at once (at the debrief): the launch is a 30 s beat and belongs at the next sector's start, under the card, not under the debrief
A real sphere element asset: the SEED-01 bus stands in; the owner's A6 has no sphere pieces yet
